title: UO vs WSU: tuition, size, location
summary: Oregon Health & Science University (UO) versus Washington State University (WSU). Also searched as WSU vs UO. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Oregon Health & Science University and Washington State University are both public institutions, but they differ significantly in size and location. Oregon Health & Science University, located in Portland, has an undergraduate enrollment of 836 students, reflecting its specialized focus. In contrast, Washington State University, situated in Pullman, enrolls 21,099 undergraduates, indicating a larger campus community. While Washington State University charges an in-state tuition of $13,391, Oregon Health & Science University does not list an undergraduate tuition figure, highlighting differences in their academic offerings and structures.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance, Oregon Health & Science University and Washington State University present distinct profiles. Washington State University charges an in-state tuition of $13,391 and an out-of-state tuition of $29,950. In contrast, Oregon Health & Science University does not provide specific undergraduate tuition figures, reflecting its specialized academic programs. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at Oregon Health & Science University is $16,625, while at Washington State University it is slightly higher, at $19,500. These differences illustrate the varied financial commitments associated with each institution.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU) in Portland, Oregon, offers a learning environment tailored to a smaller undergraduate population of 836 students, emphasizing specialized health sciences education. In contrast, Washington State University (WSU) in Pullman, Washington, supports a much larger undergraduate body of 21,099 students, providing a broader range of academic programs and campus activities. The difference in enrollment size reflects the distinct missions and campus experiences of OHSU and WSU, with OHSU focusing on health-related disciplines and WSU offering a comprehensive university setting. This contrast between OHSU and WSU highlights the varied educational models and campus communities available within the Pacific Northwest.

sections.heading: Accreditation
paragraphs: Oregon Health & Science University and Washington State University are accredited by recognized regional accrediting bodies, ensuring that their academic programs meet established standards of quality. Oregon Health & Science University, with its specialized focus on health sciences, maintains accreditation that supports its professional and graduate-level education. Washington State University, as a larger public institution, holds accreditation that covers a wide range of undergraduate and graduate programs. Both universities' accreditation status affirms their commitment to maintaining educational excellence and institutional integrity.

sections.heading: Pick UO if
paragraphs: Pick Oregon Health & Science University if you prefer a public institution with a specialized focus on health sciences and a smaller undergraduate community. While specific admission rates, in-state tuition, and completion rates are not provided for Oregon Health & Science University, its unique academic offerings distinguish it from larger public universities. In comparison, Washington State University offers a broader range of programs with a larger student body and clearly defined tuition costs. Choosing Oregon Health & Science University may suit students seeking a more focused educational environment within the public university system.

sections.heading: Pick WSU if
paragraphs: Pick Washington State University if you are looking for a public institution with a high admission rate of approximately 86.64%, indicating a more accessible entry compared to more selective universities. Washington State University charges an in-state tuition of $13,391, making it a relatively affordable option for residents. Additionally, the university has a completion rate of about 60.5% within 150% of the expected time, reflecting a moderate level of student success in finishing their degrees. These factors make Washington State University a suitable choice for students seeking a large public university with reasonable tuition and a supportive academic environment.
